messages.author: 592e7f03b854d13c
messages.subject: missing covariates
parts:
In many studies, especially in Biomedical applications, it is common to find missing covariates. Because of this there is a need to be able to deal with this without resorting to 'complete-only' data analysis. In WinBUGS it is common to assume a prior distribution for covariates and then imputation is achieved.
I was surprised to see that under FAQs there is no way to deal with missing covariates within INLA, according to the posting. 
Is there a plan to change this in the future. I would guess that this feature would limit the usefulness of INLA in biomedical applications.

you need to define a joint model for the observed and missing
observations. If that is of a 'lgm' type, you can use INLA. Recall that
in INLA, its easy to have two or more types of likelihood in the same
model. I have seen quite nice applications of this ideas, without
recalling the references.

If you have a particular model in mind, we could help you more.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] missing covariates
parts:
> I was surprised to see that under FAQs there is no way to deal with
> missing covariates within INLA, according to the posting.

The key is the second part of the FAQ answer; "No", the r-inla interface has no general-purpose method for dealing with with missing covariates, but "Yes", if you can construct a joint model for the covariates and observations, inla can estimate it for you, just as WinBUGS would.  It just needs to be specified in terms of a generalised linear model framework.

Since the type of useful covariate prior would depend entirely on the specific application, writing a general purpose interface for this would be difficult.   E.g. an "uninformative and independent" prior would likely never be useful, since then you might as well remove the corresponding observations without loosing any information, and informative priors need to be constructed using some actual information, such as dependence between covariate values.

/Finn
